--- title: "Visual attention span: letters 2" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · HVIS_CAP_VAten_LETRAS_2" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (F · Span and memory; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea HVIS_CAP_VAten_LETRAS_2`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Amplitud visoatencional: letras 2*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/HVIS_CAP_VAten_LETRAS_2.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Visual attention span: letters 2, from age 4 to 5 (1,284 administrations in 2 cohorts). AUC .50–.56 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1905 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | brief visual presentation | | Items | — | | Task family | F · Span and memory | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | Estos son los ejemplos de las pruebas que evalúan la capacidad de reconocimiento visual. Primero aparecerá un asterisco para dirigir la atención al centro de la pantalla. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework **Visual-attentional span** is the number of visual elements processed simultaneously within a string. On the platform, a string of letters, numbers or symbols is briefly presented and the child chooses what they saw. **Serial search** asks whether there is an O among groups of Qs of different sizes. The **sustained attention** task (UNED battery) consists of 50 trials in which the child decides whether the name they hear matches the picture; despite its name, the catalog describes it as an index of inhibitory control. Reading requires processing several letters at once and maintaining attention along the line. **What the evidence says:** - **Visual-attentional span predicts reading beyond phonemic awareness.** In 417 French children in Grades 1, 3 and 5, it predicted reading independently of phonemic awareness, especially for irregular words [@bosse2009span]. Orthographic depth modulates how this attention is distributed: advanced bilinguals reading in French and Basque distributed it more evenly than those reading in Spanish and Basque [@antzaka2018depth]. - **Visual search is associated with reading, with small samples.** In 16 children with dyslexia and 16 controls, slow serial search was associated with visual-attentional span and with irregular word reading, not with phonology [@lallier2013search]. Visual scanning measured in preschool predicted learning to read in Italian children [@ferretti2008scanning]. - **Sustained attention is related more to comprehension than to word reading.** In 245 poor readers in Grades 4 and 5, it explained unique variance in comprehension, but not in reading accuracy or fluency [@macdonald2021sustained]. The evidence is weaker than for phonological processes and there are almost no studies in Spanish. **What our data show.** - **Letter and symbol subtests.** With 6–10 points and a single session, AUC from .47 to .61: separately they are not interpretable. - **Numbers and letters (36 items, ages 4–5).** α = .60 and AUC of .66–.67 against persistent difficulty and of .65 against later low comprehension. It is the best in the family, as expected of alphanumeric stimuli. - **Numbers (16 items).** α = .56 and almost zero stability across school years (ρ = .05–.19). AUC from .54 to .69. - **Serial search.** α = .74, ceiling of 11–20% and AUC from .58 to .63. - **Sustained attention.** Despite an α of .95, it shows no validity: extreme ceiling (median 45 out of 50), stability of ρ = .03–.16, null correlation with the other domains and AUC from .43 to .56. It should not be used until the data have been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 2012| 154|2016/17 | 384| 384| 0| 17| | 5.1| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 900| 0| 900| 34| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.1| 384| 2012| 2.05| 1.33| 2| 0.50| 10.94| 1.04| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 4.1| 384|0–5.2 |0–6 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.1, r = .13); Phonological awareness (5.1, r = .08). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .50–.56. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .53–.54. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_CAP_VAten_LETRAS_2_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .54 (1 time point; 266–266 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 384| 2012| 0| 0| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| | 5.1| 900| 2011| 0| 1| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| **Floor effect.** At 4.1 P10 coincides with the worst possible score: many children are tied at the minimum and the norms do not distinguish between them. At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_CAP_VAten_LETRAS_2_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 272| -0.086| 0.157| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 384| 0.078| 0.448| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 380| 0.009| 0.860| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 384| 0.071| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 900| 0.002| 0.950| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 896| -0.047| 0.484| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 891| -0.015| 0.648| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 900| 0.046| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Visual attention span: letters 2” (code 1905; LEEDUCA battery) assesses visual attention span. A string of visual stimuli is briefly presented and the child reports those seen. The time limit is 20 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .53–.54. ## Pending issues - Floor effect in the norms at 4.1: at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
